 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Huchegowda, who is husband of petitioner, in a road traffic accident.

Earlier the present petition is filed by the petitioner/deceased Huchegowda, under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
During the course of trial, the petitioner has died and his legal representative came on record.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 10-12-2018 at about 7:00 p.m., the deceased petitioner by name Huchegowda was walking on the left side of Attihalli Gate road, Nuggehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District.

At that time, a motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238, being driven by its rider in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations, came from opposite side and dashed against the deceased petitioner.
Due to said impact, the deceased petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injury i.e. right dislocation fracture with speech crush injury and other injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Punya Hospital, Channarayapattna, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient and underwent surgeries.
After undergoing treatment, the deceased petitioner died due to the accidental injuries.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioner is struggling for her livelihood.
The Nuggehalli Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.

3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of the motorcycle bearing No.KA- 13-EN-3238 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner/deceased.
It has contended that, the alleged accident has occurred on 10-12- 2018, but the complaint has been lodged on 13-12-2018, there was three days delay in lodging the complaint.

It has denied the involvement of the offending motorcycle in the alleged accident, the petitioner in collusion with owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 and the police have falsely implicated the said vehicle in the alleged accident, in order to have wrongful gain from the insurance company.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

In the additional written statement the respondent No.2 has further contended that, the petitioner namely Huchegowda has died on 11-10-2020 and the petitioner No.1(a) is not the legal heir/wife of the deceased Huchegowda.
She has not produced any document to show that, she is the legal heir/wife of the deceased.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the deceased Huchegowda S/o late Thimmegowda has succumbed to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident,
alleged to have occurred on 10-12-2018 at about 7.00 p.m., on the left side of Attihalli Gate road, Nuggehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN- 3238 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.
Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the respondent No.1, who is owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN-3238.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company though has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the deceased petitioner in collusion with the owner of said vehicle and the police has falsely implicated the said vehicle in the alleged accident, in order to have wrongful gain from the insurance company and the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident, has failed to establish the said contentions.

There is absolutely no evidence adduced by the respondent No.2 to establish the said contentions or to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner with respect to cause of accident.
Even, the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in its written statement on oath.

On the other hand, the P.W.1 and P.W.2 have clearly deposed in their evidence that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 and dashing the same to the deceased P.W.1, who was walking on the left side of the road.

Further, the P.W.1 and P.W.2 have unequivocally denied the suggestion made to them that, the said accident has occurred due to self fall of P.W.1 and not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238.

Further, they have unequivocally denied the suggestion that, the deceased petitioner in collusion with the owner of said vehicle and the police has falsely implicated the said vehicle in the alleged accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 & P.W.2 in length

, nothing worth has been elicited from their mouth which establishes that, the accident in question has occurred due to self fall of P.W.1 and not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 or the said vehicle has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
The oral evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8 and 14, it clearly reveals that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA- 13-EN-3238 and dashing the same to the deceased P.W.1, who was walking on the left side of the road.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet,
which is marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 and the deceased Huchegowda has sustained grievous injury on the right side of his hip in the said accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.2 spot mahazer also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 12 feet wide Nuggehalli-Attihalli road, near Attihalli gate, Nuggehalli Hobli,
Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 and dashing the same to deceased pedestrian.
Further, as per Ex.P.4 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident had not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not occurred due to the any Huchegowda vs Ranjitha N.U on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11071342/
5 mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
It is pertinent to note that, as per Ex.P.4 the front portion parts of the offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-13- EN-3238 have been damaged.

If really as contended by the respondent No.2, if the said vehicle was not at all involved in the accident, the immediate question that arises is, how the front portion parts of the said motorcycle got damaged.
It is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the said damage were already present before the date and time of the accident in question or the same were caused in some other accident.
14. No doubt, there is a delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint in respect of accident in question, by the brother- in-law of deceased Huchegowda.

It is settled proposition of law that, mere delay in lodging the complaint in a motor accident claim cases is not fatal, if adequate explanation for delay is offered and it should not be a ground to reject the claim petition.
It gains relevance in the cases where other evidence does not support the claimant's allegations.

In the present case, it is clearly stated in the Ex.P.1 first information statement/complaint that, as nobody came forward from the side of rider of offending vehicle to bear the medical expenses of the injured and even they did not come forward for settlement and as the informant was engaged in providing treatment to the injured, there is a delay caused in lodging the complaint.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the said version.

There is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that,
the reason for delay stated in the Ex.P.1 is false and concocted and even nothing with respect to same has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 & 2.

Further, it is pertinent to note that,
the Ex.R.1 MLC register extract issued by Punya Hospital, Channarayapatna and Ex.R.2 MLC extract issued by the Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, clearly goes to show that, on the very day of accident i.e. 10-10-2018 the medico-legal case has been registered at Punya Hospital,
Channarayapatna and on 11-10-2018 it is registered at Janapriya Hospital, Hassan.

It is settled proposition of law that, it is the duty of concerned doctor or the hospital authorities to inform the jurisdictional police with regard to medico-legal case registered at their hospital immediately without any delay and after receiving such information the concerned police have to visit the hospital at the earliest and record the statement of the injured or his legal representatives.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the reasons for delay stated in Ex.P.1 first information statement and hold that, the delay caused in lodging the complaint in the present case has been properly and adequately explained.

15. Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 medical certificate and Ex.P.15 lab reports, clearly speaks that, the deceased petitioner Huchegowda had sustained grievous injury i.e. right trochantric fracture in the road traffic accident.

Further, the Ex.P.9 discharge summary issued by Janapriya Hospital clearly speaks that, on 11-12-2018 the injured Huchegowda was brought to the hospital with history right hip joint pain, swelling, tenderness and restricted movements and he has been treated in the said hospital as an in-patient from 11-12-2018 to 24-11-2018.

Further it reveals that, the deceased Huchegowda has undergone surgery for the said injury i.e. ORIF with P. F. Nailing is done with implant fixation and he was discharged with an advise for follow up treatment for the restricted fracture movements and not to involve in any strenuous activities.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 insurance company though has denied the authenticity of said documents, has not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the Huchegowda vs Ranjitha N.U on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11071342/
6 deceased Huchegowda has not sustained the above said injury and the medical records produced by the petitioners are false.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN-3238 in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle and the injuries caused to deceased Huchegowda in the said accident.
16.
As noted above there is sufficient evidence available on record to show that, the deceased Huchegowda has sustained grievous injury on the right side of his hip in the accident in question.

But, there is absolutely no oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner to show that, the deceased Huchegowda has died due to said injury or any other injuries sustained in the said accident.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, after undergoing treatment for 14 days at Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, as an in-patient, he was discharged from the hospital on 24-12-2018.
Further, Huchegowda has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, after discharge from the Hospital he has taken follow up treatment for just 4 times.
After lapse of 2 years from the date of discharge from the hospital, Huchegowda has died.
As per Ex.P.16 death certificate he has died on 11-10-2020.

There is absolutely no material on record to show that, after discharge from the Janapriya Hospital till the date of his death Huchegowda was under follow up treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident and he has succumbed to the said injuries.
There is no nexus between the injuries sustained by Huchegoda in the accident and cause of his death.
The petitioner has neither examined any doctor, nor she has produced any document to show that, deceased Huchegowda has died due to the injuries sustained in the accident in question.
Even, there is no post-mortem report produced by the petitioner in the case to establish the cause of his death.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to hold that, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the deceased Huchegowda has died due to injuries sustained in the accident in question.
17. It is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

19. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Huchegowda has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 10- 12-2018 at about 7.00 p.m., on the left side of Attihalli Gate road, Nugehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent Huchegowda vs Ranjitha N.U on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11071342/
7 riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN-3238.
But, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the deceased Huchgowda has died due to injuries sustained in the said accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioners have successfully proved that, the deceased petitioner Huchegowda has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident occurred on 10-12-2018 at about 7.00 p.m.,
on Attihalli Gate road, Nugehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN-3238.

If the deceased Huchegowda had been alive he would have been entitled for pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.

But, unfortunately as he has died during the course of trial, the issue with regard to assessment and granting compensation under the heads; loss of future earning,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc., does not survive for consideration.

But, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record clearly goes to show that,
the deceased Huchegowda has undergone treatment for a period of 14 days, from 11-12-2018 to 24-12-2018, in Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, for the grievous injuries sustained in the said accident and has expended huge amount towards medical expenses.

In such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner being the legal representative/wife of deceased Huchegowda, is entitled for the pecuniary damages, such as expenses for medical treatment, attendants and conveyance, due to grievous injuries caused to the deceased in the said accident.

i) Medical expenses: The deceased petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 69 medical bills, which are marked as Ex.P.11.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,41,554/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,41,554/- under the head of medical expenses.
ii) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the deceased petitioner Huchegowda has taken treatment as an in-patient for 14 days, from 11-12-2018 to 24-12-2018, in Janapriya Hospital,
Hassan.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 14 = Rs.14,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
iii) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the deceased petitioner Huchegowda has taken treatment as an in-patient for 14 days, from 11-12-2018 to 24-12-2018, in Janapriya Hospital, Hassan.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 14 = Rs.11,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
iv) Conveyance expenses:

8

Huchegowda is the resident of Bananakere Village,
Nuggehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, the accident has taken place on Attihalli Gate road, Nugehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District and he has taken treatment at Janapriya Hospital, Hassan.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

21. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1.
Medical expenses Rs. 1,41,554-00 2. Attendant charges 14,000-00
3. Food and nourishment 11,200-00 4. Conveyance expenses 10,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,76,754/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum,
from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN-3238 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,76,754/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,76,754/- (Rupees one lakh seventy six thousand seven hundred and fifty four only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.facts:
During the course of trial, the petitioner has died and his legal representative came on record.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the deceased Huchegowda S/o late Thimmegowda has succumbed to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident,
alleged to have occurred on 10-12-2018 at about 7.00 p.m., on the left side of Attihalli Gate road, Nuggehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN- 3238 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company though has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EN-3238 is not at all involved in the alleged accident and the deceased petitioner in collusion with the owner of said vehicle and the police has falsely implicated the said vehicle in the alleged accident, in order to have wrongful gain from the insurance company and the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident, has failed to establish the said contentions.
It is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the said damage were already present before the date and time of the accident in question or the same were caused in some other accident.
14. No doubt, there is a delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint in respect of accident in question, by the brother- in-law of deceased Huchegowda.
It is settled proposition of law that, mere delay in lodging the complaint in a motor accident claim cases is not fatal, if adequate explanation for delay is offered and it should not be a ground to reject the claim petition.
It gains relevance in the cases where other evidence does not support the claimant's allegations.
In the present case, it is clearly stated in the Ex.P.1 first information statement/complaint that, as nobody came forward from the side of rider of offending vehicle to bear the medical expenses of the injured and even they did not come forward for settlement and as the informant was engaged in providing treatment to the injured, there is a delay caused in lodging the complaint.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the said version.
There is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that,
the reason for delay stated in the Ex.P.1 is false and concocted and even nothing with respect to same has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 & 2.
It is settled proposition of law that, it is the duty of concerned doctor or the hospital authorities to inform the jurisdictional police with regard to medico-legal case registered at their hospital immediately without any delay and after receiving such information the concerned police have to visit the hospital at the earliest and record the statement of the injured or his legal representatives.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the reasons for delay stated in Ex.P.1 first information statement and hold that, the delay caused in lodging the complaint in the present case has been properly and adequately explained.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-13-EN-3238 in the accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle and the injuries caused to deceased Huchegowda in the said accident.
16.
But, there is absolutely no oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner to show that, the deceased Huchegowda has died due to said injury or any other injuries sustained in the said accident.
After lapse of 2 years from the date of discharge from the hospital, Huchegowda has died.
There is absolutely no material on record to show that, after discharge from the Janapriya Hospital till the date of his death Huchegowda was under follow up treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident and he has succumbed to the said injuries.
There is no nexus between the injuries sustained by Huchegoda in the accident and cause of his death.
The petitioner has neither examined any doctor, nor she has produced any document to show that, deceased Huchegowda has died due to the injuries sustained in the accident in question.
Even, there is no post-mortem report produced by the petitioner in the case to establish the cause of his death.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to hold that, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the deceased Huchegowda has died due to injuries sustained in the accident in question.
17. It is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
opennyai_summary.decision:
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
21. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1.
Medical expenses Rs. 1,41,554-00 2. Attendant charges 14,000-00
Total Rs. 1,76,754-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,76,754/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum,
from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,76,754/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,76,754/- (Rupees one lakh seventy six thousand seven hundred and fifty four only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
